verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; no STOP (no UB, ABI regression or hidden obligation); three defects repaired (one sizing error and two authority-UB reproductions)
scope: Per-file audit of the eight legacy EVP cipher carriers at the head of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt: AES-CBC-HMAC-SHA256, Blowfish, CAST5, single DES, IDEA, RC4-HMAC-MD5, RC4 and SEED. Seven files are clean transcriptions; the stitched AES-CBC-HMAC-SHA256 control carried the SHA-1 digest constant, and the two AEAD controls reproduced the authority's negative-length fault.

defects.class: compatibility / caller buffer sizing (wrong digest constant)
defects.description: EVP_CTRL_TLS1_1_MULTIBLOCK_MAX_BUFSIZE answered 5 + 16 + ((arg + 20 + 16) & -16), the SHA-1 row's formula, instead of the SHA-256 row's 5 + 16 + ((arg + 32 + 16) & -16) (e_aes_cbc_hmac_sha256.c:807-808 in 1.1.1w, 3.0.0, 3.4.8, 3.5.9 and 3.6.4). For arg = 16384 the answer was 16437 rather than 16453, so a caller sizing a multiblock output buffer from this control could be sixteen bytes short.
defects.fix: Extract tls11_multiblock_max_bufsize(arg), use SHA256_DIGEST_LENGTH (32), and refuse an overflowing fragment size with -1 rather than relying on the authority's undefined signed addition.
defects.witness: evp::e_aes_cbc_hmac_sha256::tests::the_tls11_max_bufsize_reserves_a_sha256_digest and the_tls11_max_bufsize_refuses_overflow (both pass). Cross-checked against five authority releases and against the provider's aesni_cbc_hmac_sha256_tls1_multiblock_max_bufsize, which already used 32.

defects.description: EVP_CTRL_AEAD_SET_MAC_KEY with a negative arg fell into the else arm and called ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(ptr_, hmac_key, arg as usize), a huge read. The authority's memcpy makes the same int-to-size_t conversion and faults; a negative key length is never a valid call.
defects.fix: Refuse arg < 0 with -1 before any pointer use (§17).
defects.witness: Code and compile review; no in-tree fixture constructs a legacy RC4-HMAC-MD5 context for this private control, so the guard has no runtime test (recorded as NOT_RUN).

defects.description: The legacy SET_MAC_KEY arm forwarded a negative arg to the provider's size_t length, and MULTIBLOCK_ENCRYPT dereferenced the parameter block without the size test its _AAD sibling makes. Both are undefined in the authority for invalid arguments and were reachable through the legacy callback.
defects.fix: SET_MAC_KEY refuses arg < 0 with -1; MULTIBLOCK_ENCRYPT refuses arg < size_of::<EvpCtrlTls11MultiblockParam>() with -1, matching the provider arm's recorded deliberate divergence.
defects.witness: Code and compile review; no in-tree fixture constructs the legacy context (NOT_RUN for a runtime control).

contracts_reused: Legacy EVP_CIPHER callback contract: init/do_cipher/ctrl callers supply a live EVP_CIPHER_CTX whose cipher_data block has at least the cipher's ctx_size (RC-1-adjacent, audited in src/evp/cipher_ctx.rs)

OB-3/OB-4 shared owned-context release: EVP_CIPHER_CTX_reset cleanses cipher_data with OPENSSL_cleanse(cipher_data, ctx_size) before CRYPTO_free, so every key schedule in these files is cleansed on release without a per-file cleanup callback
Secret-scratch cleansing (B19 technique): hmac_key[64] in RC4-HMAC-MD5 and in the provider set_mac_key, plus IDEA's decrypt temporary, are cleansed before return
AES-CBC-HMAC-SHA256 provider construction contract (ProvAesHmacSha256Ctx layout, sync_in direction/IV copy, provider cipher/ctrl bodies) reused rather than duplicated
Authority differential contract for the legacy static initialisers: nid, block_size, key_len, iv_len, flags, origin, ASN.1 views and ctx_size field for field
residuals: The AES-CBC-HMAC-SHA256 legacy callbacks use the provider's 840-byte ProvAesHmacSha256Ctx as cipher_data rather than the authority's ~608-byte EVP_AES_HMAC_SHA256. The block is allocated and cleansed at that exact size and every callback agrees on the layout; the difference is not ABI-visible because EVP_CIPHER is opaque and the provider fetch replaces the method before a normal EVP_EncryptInit_ex path uses ctx_size. An engine path (Phase 13) is the only way to reach the legacy ctx_size.
The legacy ctrl callbacks remain reachable only through an engine; no in-tree test constructs such a context, so M54-D2/D3 have no runtime witness.

Adjacent observation, not edited: the already-audited src/evp/e_aes_cbc_hmac_sha1.rs (AUDITED-FILES.txt:282) has the same negative SET_MAC_KEY and undersized MULTIBLOCK_ENCRYPT patterns at :191 and :255. Its MAX_BUFSIZE constant is already the correct SHA-1 20. Queue a follow-up with the same two guards.
No constant-time claim is made for any of these carriers; the stitching and MAC comparison paths reuse provider bodies whose timing discipline is not measured in this batch.
